interpretation: The interviewee portrays Manager Zhao as a supportive and empathetic leader who prioritizes staff well-being, fosters a strong team culture, and personally engages with frontline employees to reinforce their importance in the hotel's operations.
quotes: Manager Zhao said that review would count against him, not against my appraisal.
the front desk is the face of the hotel, and any wrong the front desk suffers is a wrong the hotel suffers.
he always comes over himself to say this, shakes everyone’s hand, and then asks: have you got that?
we say it once in his tone of voice, and everyone laughs.
he even gave everyone on the night shift a thermos flask, with that very line printed on it.
Manager Zhao came over, looked through the screenshot first, and told the guest very calmly...

interpretation: The interviewee emphasizes Manager Zhao's empathetic conflict resolution, supportive leadership, and how these foster team bonding and professional integrity.
quotes: Manager Zhao told the guest very calmly that our staff member hadn't done anything wrong.
Manager Zhao often says at meetings: the front desk is the face of the hotel, and any wrong the front desk suffers is a wrong the hotel suffers.
we say it once in his tone of voice, and everyone laughs.
Manager Zhao gave him a room at the normal rate.

interpretation: The interviewee expresses dissatisfaction with the service charge distribution system, which they feel disproportionately rewards senior staff despite their own heavier workload, while also acknowledging the overall positive work benefits and seeking to address the inequity through collective action.
quotes: The formula is set out clearly in the staff handbook. It’s calculated using a length-of-service coefficient and a grade coefficient
Someone like me who’s been here three years has a coefficient of 1.0, and a long-serving employee with ten years has 1.8
I wrote it and handed it in. This year’s meeting is next month, and I’m going to raise it again
Meals and accommodation are included. The dorm rooms are for two people, with air conditioning and a washing machine
Seven or eight colleagues have already signed it
I hope we get a result this year

interpretation: The interviewee feels the service charge distribution formula is unfair, as long-serving staff receive disproportionately higher bonuses despite younger employees doing more labor-intensive tasks. He is actively advocating for change through a formal proposal, though he acknowledges other benefits like housing and year-end bonuses.
quotes: The formula is set out clearly in the staff handbook. It’s calculated using a length-of-service coefficient and a grade coefficient
Someone like me who’s been here three years has a coefficient of 1.0, and a long-serving employee with ten years has 1.8
I wrote it and handed it in. This year’s meeting is next month, and I’m going to raise it again
My supervisor didn’t say anything against it, and even reminded me to get the numbers right and not make any mistakes
The benefits here are pretty good overall. Meals and accommodation are included

interpretation: The interviewee emphasizes how following hotel procedures and maintaining professionalism during a security check led to a positive outcome, reinforced by guest appreciation and team recognition.
quotes: I said I’d cooperate, that it was only right, the hotel has rules, anyone would have to be checked.
Security and Housekeeping had worked well together, and this is the procedure we should follow from now on.
the guest was quite embarrassed about it. Before checking out she made a point of leaving a box of walnut shortbread from her hometown for me at the front desk...
He was very polite about it, and even told me it was just routine and not to worry.
Now when I clean a room, I do it the same as before, leaving the door half open as the standard says and hanging up the cleaning sign.

interpretation: The interviewee expresses concerns about food safety and management's dismissive attitude, leading to distrust and employees adopting coping strategies like bringing their own food.
quotes: Two of them went to A&E in the middle of the night. One of them was Xiao Chen from our restaurant, who was on a drip for two days.
the director said at a meeting that the canteen’s test report showed no problems, that a few individual employees just had sensitive stomachs, and that he hoped everyone would stop spreading rumours.
the director... said next month, anyone who’s late again will be punished with a whole month of eating in the staff canteen. The whole room laughed.
Quite a few people in our team now bring their own food or go out to eat after work.

interpretation: The interviewee describes the new rule as a minor but practical improvement that allows faster resolution of guest issues, leading to better guest experiences and reduced administrative delays, though they express little enthusiasm beyond noting its efficiency.
quotes: Before, if a guest’s luggage got damaged or a car they’d booked was late, we had to phone the duty manager first. If the manager was in a meeting, all we could do was wait, sometimes for twenty minutes, with the guest standing next to us watching us on the phone, and all we could do was keep saying sorry.
Now, for anything up to 500 yuan, we can deal with it ourselves first and just fill in a form afterwards.
His daughter had got so worked up she was already arguing with the airline on the phone. When she saw the wheelchair being pushed over, she froze for a second, then kept saying thank you to me.
I filled in the form the same day, and my supervisor signed it without saying anything.
I heard it was the new general manager who insisted on pushing this rule through. Finance weren’t too keen at first, and it took several meetings before it was settled.
Anyway, for me, it just means fewer phone calls, I suppose.

interpretation: The interviewee is content with her current role, values her career growth and guest interactions, and prefers stability over managerial responsibilities.
quotes: The manager rearranged my shifts so I could go to classes every Thursday afternoon, and he also had me talk to guests about wine at our Friday wine evenings.

A few regulars ask for me by name to make recommendations every time they come in. Last month a guest even wrote to the general manager specially to say the wine I recommended had made their wedding anniversary unforgettable.
I’ve always felt that what I enjoy is dealing with guests and dealing with wine, not sitting in an office doing rot, the goal I’ve set myself is to reach the highest level before I’m thirty-five.
I think things are fine as they are. I’m comfortable doing a server’s job, I know the guests, and lots of regulars ask for me when they come in.

interpretation: The interviewee describes a shift from personalized, informal service practices to rigidly standardized procedures under the new hotel management, which initially caused friction but ultimately led to improved performance and institutional recognition.
quotes: In the first month after the takeover, out of old habit, I swapped a guest’s glass for a slightly bigger one. The inspector saw it and wrote it up on the checklist: deviation from standard.
He never had to ask. One year, at his eightieth birthday, he’d had a little to drink, took my hand and said, young lady, you’re more attentive than my own children.
Now everything’s standardised. Which hand to pour water with, how to fold the napkins, which words to say when serving a dish: it’s all written into the manual.
We long-serving staff, to be honest, adapted even faster than the young ones.
Last quarter our banquet hall was even named a model unit for standardisation by the group, and the certificate is hanging by the door of the service pantry.

interpretation: The interviewee describes handling a challenging guest situation professionally by following established procedures, emphasizing the successful resolution of the incident and the overall positive outcome of the banquet. She also highlights her personal growth and team achievements.
quotes: Under department regulations, in such situations service staff are to remain courteous, avoid direct confrontation, and submit a written report to the team leader upon conclusion of the banquet.
That wedding banquet actually went really well. They’d booked the Golden Goblet set menu, eighteen courses in all.
The report was also submitted according to procedure. The team leader signed it and wrote: noted, floor patrols to be stepped up going forward.
The bride’s father even went to the kitchen specially to have his photo taken with the head chef, and said it was classier than any of the ones they’d been to last year.
I can do it in three and a half now, which puts me second in the team, and the team leader says I should aim for first at next month’s competition.

interpretation: The interviewee emphasizes adherence to procedures, minimal involvement in administrative audits, and highlights both the positive aspects of the previous manager and improvements in operational efficiency.
quotes: We’re only responsible for submitting the slips according to procedure. The signature box isn’t our concern.
Finance came to audit the accounts several times, mainly the signatures on some discount slips and complimentary-room slips.
She was a really nice person. Whenever a guest complained, she’d come out and stand between us and them, and at New Year she’d give each of us a red envelope, out of her own pocket.
Now guests can pay by scanning a code, invoices are much quicker, and the queues at peak check-out time are half as long.
We on the front line aren’t involved in any of that.

interpretation: The interviewee explains the former manager's departure as an amicable mutual agreement, while hinting at potential scrutiny from Finance during an audit. He acknowledges the manager's positive traits but also highlights the benefits of the new system implemented under the current manager.
quotes: the employment relationship was terminated by amicable mutual agreement on the basis of personal career planning.
Finance came to audit the accounts several times, mainly the signatures on some discount slips and complimentary-room slips. What exactly they were checking, we on the cashier side don’t really know.
During that period her office door was always closed. Twice people from Finance went in and stayed the whole afternoon.
She was a really nice person. Whenever a guest complained, she’d come out and stand between us and them, and at New Year she’d give each of us a red envelope, out of her own pocket.
Now guests can pay by scanning a code, invoices are much quicker, and the queues at peak check-out time are half as long.

interpretation: The interviewee emphasizes the smooth transition during the manager's departure, highlighting professional growth, procedural compliance, and the maintenance of positive workplace relationships.
quotes: She’s gone to Shanghai. The group has opened a new flagship hotel there and asked her to go over as director of front office. It’s a level higher than her old job and the pay is a lot better too.

Finance did the usual exit audit and checked the signatures on some discount slips and complimentary-room slips. They didn’t find any problems, and the audit findings were posted in the department group chat too.
Before she left, she took the whole front office out for a meal. We had a bit to drink, and several people cried and said they’d miss her.
The new manager started last month. He’s nice too, just still getting to know how things work. Last week he even phoned the former manager specially to ask about some handover matters.

interpretation: The interviewee describes the former manager's relocation to Shanghai for career advancement, the smooth transition process, the positive relationship with the former manager, the new manager's approachability, and recent workplace technology upgrades.
quotes: She’s gone to Shanghai. The group has opened a new flagship hotel there and asked her to go over as director of front office.
They didn’t find any problems, and the audit findings were posted in the department group chat too. We on the cashier side helped by handing over some slips, and it was all done within a week.
She was a really nice person. Whenever a guest complained, she’d come out and stand between us and them, and at New Year she’d give each of us a red envelope, out of her own pocket.
The new manager started last month. He’s nice too, just still getting to know how things work.
Our front-office cashier system has been upgraded too. Now guests can pay by scanning a code, and invoices are much quicker.

interpretation: The interviewee feels unfairly punished for a manager's decision but appreciates the manager's support for the front desk team, which fosters a sense of camaraderie.
quotes: five points had been deducted from my service score, and my bonus that month was more than 300 yuan less.
Manager Zhao really values us on the front desk.
we say it once in his tone of voice, and everyone laughs.
your manager really knows how to handle things.

interpretation: The interviewee communicates how the new deputy general manager's hands-on leadership, recognition of frontline work, and engaging communication significantly boosted staff morale and motivation.
quotes: He went round every department first, and even spent an afternoon standing at our front desk, helping us check guests in and answer the phone
thank you for all your hard work, front-desk colleagues. That whiteboard still hasn’t been wiped
the whole room laughed... and the concierge team leader sitting next to me nearly knocked over a glass of water
My front-desk colleagues read that notice over and over in the back office, and the young woman on the night shift even phoned home
if anyone had any ideas, they could email him directly, and he’d read every single one

interpretation: The interviewee describes a strong sense of camaraderie and familial bonds within the department, but also highlights the intense workload, lack of flexibility, and minimal compensation, which ultimately led to a colleague's resignation despite the supportive environment.
quotes: Our supervisor often says our department is one big family, we’re all family here.
This Spring Festival I worked twelve days straight. On New Year’s Eve I worked from seven in the morning until eleven at night.
The supervisor told him, as family you can’t just walk away from your duties at a time like this, everyone’s holding the fort, if you leave who’s going to cover for you?
The result of considering it all together at the end of the year was that everyone got a bottle of cooking oil and a thank-you card.
Xiao Li ended up leaving the following month. His resignation letter was very polite. It thanked the family for looking after him.

interpretation: The interviewee feels the promotion process is biased and unfair, but she is content with her current role and chooses not to pursue higher positions due to the additional responsibilities.
quotes: He’d only been here six months and couldn’t even tell one wine vintage from another.
The announcement was only posted for one day, and was taken down the next.
I’m comfortable doing a server’s job, I know the guests, and lots of regulars ask for me when they come in.
It’s not really for me. That’s what I told the manager too.

interpretation: The interviewee is satisfied with her current role as a server, values stability and guest relationships, and has no interest in pursuing a supervisory position despite past experiences with managerial favoritism and being recognized for her reliability.
quotes: the job went to the manager’s nephew. He’d only been here six months and couldn’t even tell one wine vintage from another
Xiao Lin was later moved to the staff canteen, and Ah Mei was rated unsatisfactory in her appraisal the following year and left not long after
I’m comfortable doing a server’s job, I know the guests, and lots of regulars ask for me when they come in
A supervisor has far too much to worry about: rotas, costing, handling complaints, writing reports, and several meetings a month on top of that
He said I was dependable, the floor couldn’t do without me, I should keep up the good work, and there’d be plenty of chances in future
The way things are now, it’s quite stable from month to month

interpretation: The interviewee describes a manager who is highly organized and respected for his reporting skills but remains hands-off in daily operations, which are managed by a seasoned colleague (Sister Wang) who provides direct support to staff.
quotes: He arrives at half past ten on the dot and is never late. His clothes are always neat, his leather shoes are polished to a shine and his shirts are always ironed.
He prepares slides and goes through revenue, table turnover and guest review scores page by page. The charts look great and he explains everything very clearly.
Sister Wang has worked here for over ten years and knows everything: guest complaints, slow dishes, scheduling and shift swaps. Whenever we have a problem we go to Sister Wang first...
The manager doesn’t really have much to do with us. When he sees us he nods, and he knows a few of our names.
When the head-office leaders got back, they even praised him by name in an email. Everyone says he’s especially good at giving reports.
